exposure: Perineal protection bundle (PPB) implementation (warm compresses in the second stage, controlled hands-on birth, specific technique for episiotomy, routine rectal examination and grading of perineal tears by two experienced clinicians)
cohort: The study included all women who had their first vaginal birth between 2016 and June 2023.
finding: The study identified a 40% reduction (3.3% absolute reduction) in OASI rates following the introduction of the perineal protection bundle, but no significant reduction in anal incontinence.
mod_finding: There was an increase in the episiotomy rate from 48% to 56% (OR 1.37), mostly for vacuum-assisted births, with no significant increase for normal vaginal births, and no change in caesarean sections at full dilatation.
followup_time: 6 weeks and 6 months (for anal incontinence in OASI cases)
